Foothill Blvd.; Azusa Police Department Lobby - 725 N. Alameda Ave., and the City of Azusa Web Page www.azusaca.gov.
Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

None.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez thanked staff for a successful Night Market; reminded the community that Foothill
Transit will be providing transportation to the Rose Parade via the A Line; and asked for prayers for the soldiers
in Syria who were killed in an ambush, as well as the Brown University students who were killed.

Councilmember Avila announced the “Holiday Melodies” event on December 17; thanked the City Manager
and Staff for the successful projects; and expressed appreciation to the City Clerk’s Office for the beautiful
holiday decorations in the auditorium.

Councilmember Mendez announced “Family Bingo Night” on December 16; invited the community to attend
the upcoming “Azusa Santa Tour”; and thanked the City Manager and Staff for the successful events held over
the past six weeks.

Councilmember Bow announced the Teen DIY Crafts Upside Down event; reminded the community not to
drink and drive during the holiday season; and wished all those who celebrate a happy Chanukah.

Mayor Gonzales thanked the City Manager and Staff for the successful events held during the month of
December, complimented staff on the holiday decorations, expressed appreciation to his colleagues for a
wonderful year, and wished everyone a happy holiday season.

CONSIDERATION OF TERMINATING A SERVICE CONTRACT WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY
ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL

Lieutenant Vasconcelos provided an overview for the termination of LA County Animal Care and Control;
mentioned that City of Azusa has maintained a longstanding relationship with them; stated that the standard of
service has declined and expressed that residents deserve better service for the amount they are paying.

Councilmembers asked questions regarding the location of the proposed new animal control facility and
anticipated response times. Staff responded that the facility is in Pomona and clarified that the primary concern
was not response time, but rather that LA County Animal Care and Control had, at times, not responded to calls
for service.

City Manager Gonzalez added that rates have nearly doubled since the City began contracting with LA County
Animal Control; noted that Inland Valley Humane Society & SPCA provides quality service and currently
serves several surrounding cities; explained that staff is requesting Council authorization to provide the required
six-month notice to LA County to terminate the contract.

Moved by Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez , seconded by Councilmember Avila and carried by the following vote of
the Council, to authorize staff to provide Los Angeles County Animal Care and Control with notice of
termination as required under the County agreement; and direct staff to commence negotiations with Inland
Valley Humane Society for Animal Care and Control Services Commencing July 1, 2026; and return to Council
with an update no later than March 2026.
